papers.title: An oral coral-like resveratrol nanocomplex protects against dry eye disease through ocular and systemic redox homeostasis.
papers.abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is a progressive ocular disorder in which chronic inflammation and oxidative stress synergistically damage ocular tissues and impair vision. While topical anti-inflammatory and artificial tears therapies are the standard treatment for DED, their long-term application is limited by adverse effects and poor patient compliance. Emerging evidence suggests that systemic redox dysregulation contributes to DED pathogenesis, highlighting the potential of oral antioxidant intervention as a disease-modifying strategy. However, the clinical translation of oral antioxidants has been
papers.summary: This study develops an oral coral-like resveratrol nanocomplex designed to restore redox homeostasis both in the eye and systemically, offering a potential disease-modifying treatment for dry eye disease. The approach addresses the limitations of topical therapies by targeting the systemic oxidative stress that contributes to DED pathogenesis.

papers.title: Symbiotic interactions and climate change implications of the octocoral microbiome.
papers.abstract: Octocorals are vital components of tropical, temperate, and cold-water benthic marine ecosystems. Their associated microbiomes, comprising microeukaryotes, prokaryotes, and viruses, are increasingly recognised as central to host health, nutrient cycling, and chemical defence. Metagenomics and amplicon sequencing have uncovered taxonomic and functional complexity within these microbial communities, revealing patterns of host specificity and health status, along with seasonality and geographic structuring. However, anthropogenic stressors, particularly those associated with global climate change
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on the microbiomes of octocorals, which include microeukaryotes, prokaryotes, and viruses that support host health, nutrient cycling, and chemical defense. It highlights how metagenomics and amplicon sequencing have revealed host-specific microbial patterns linked to health, seasonality, and geography, while emphasizing threats from climate change.

papers.title: The canine gut microbiome as a translational model for human health and aging.
papers.abstract: The domestic dog is increasingly recognized as a complementary translational model for microbiome research relevant to human health while also offering direct benefits for veterinary medicine. Dogs share environments and dietary exposures with humans and show substantial taxonomic and gene-content similarity to the human gut microbiome, although the apparent degree of similarity depends strongly on whether read recruitment, gene-catalog overlap, or functional overlap is assessed. Dogs also develop spontaneous chronic enteropathies, obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction, cancers, cognitive d
papers.summary: This review argues that the domestic dog is a valuable translational model for studying the gut microbiome's role in human health and aging, given shared environments, diets, and substantial taxonomic and functional similarity to the human gut microbiome. It notes that the apparent degree of similarity depends heavily on the analytical approach used (read recruitment, gene-catalog overlap, or functional overlap), and highlights that dogs naturally develop chronic enteropathies, obesity-related metabolic dysfunction, cancers, and cognitive decline relevant to human conditions.

papers.title: Metagenomic insights into pathogen diversity and public health risk of Haemaphysalis longicornis in Gansu Province of China.
papers.abstract: The tick Haemaphysalis longicornis vectors numerous zoonotic pathogens, yet its pathogen diversity and associated spatial health risks are not fully characterized. To profile this vector, we performed metagenomic sequencing on 290 H. longicornis ticks across 29 sites in Gansu Province, China. We resolved 25 bacterial and one protozoan genera, with computational analyses revealing population-level distribution patterns and identifying environmental factors as key drivers of spatial variation.We detected marker genes associated with 12 pathogenic microorganisms. Alongside established threats (Ri
papers.summary: This study used metagenomic sequencing of 290 Haemaphysalis longicornis ticks from 29 sites in Gansu Province, China, to characterize the pathogens they carry. The authors identified 25 bacterial and one protozoan genera, detected marker genes for 12 pathogenic microorganisms, and found that environmental factors drive spatial variation in pathogen distribution. The work maps tick-borne pathogen diversity and highlights public health risks in this region.

papers.title: Metax enables accurate cross-domain taxonomic profiling of metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Taxonomic profiling is fundamental to microbiome research, yet achieving high species-level accuracy remains challenging for complex communities that span bacteria, viruses, eukaryotes, and archaea, and these limitations are exacerbated in low-biomass, host-dominated samples. We introduce Metax, a cross-domain taxonomic profiler that integrates coverage-based probabilistic modeling with an expectation-maximization framework to distinguish true microbial signals from artifacts. Across >600 samples from host-associated, environmental, wastewater, and low-biomass clinical settings, including benc
papers.summary: Metax is a new cross-domain taxonomic profiler for metagenomes that combines coverage-based probabilistic modeling with an expectation-maximization framework to improve species-level accuracy across bacteria, viruses, eukaryotes, and archaea. It was validated on over 600 samples spanning host-associated, environmental, wastewater, and low-biomass clinical settings, where it distinguishes true microbial signals from artifacts.

papers.title: Landscape of retron diversity across the SPIRE microbial metagenome resource reveals candidate novel type XI-like lineages.
papers.abstract: Retrons are bacterial genetic elements encoding a specialized reverse transcriptase (RT) that synthesizes multicopy single-stranded DNA and are increasingly recognized as components of bacterial anti-phage defense systems. However, their diversity and ecological distribution across large-scale genomic resources remain poorly characterized. Here, we surveyed retron RTs across the SPIRE representative metagenome collection, a non-redundant, species-level data set spanning diverse microbial habitats. Using a curated panel of type-specific hidden Markov models, we identified retrons representing a
papers.summary: This study surveyed retron reverse transcriptases across the SPIRE metagenome collection, a large non-redundant species-level resource spanning diverse microbial habitats. Using curated type-specific hidden Markov models, the authors cataloged retron diversity and identified candidate novel type XI-like lineages. The work expands understanding of retron ecological distribution and highlights their potential roles in bacterial anti-phage defense.

papers.title: VISTA: a classifier for metagenomic subspecies and community state typing of the vaginal microbiome.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic community state types (mgCSTs) capture within-species genetic and functional diversity and community structure of the vaginal microbiome, enabling precise links between microbiome composition, function, and health-related risk. VISTA, the Vaginal Inference of Subspecies and Typing Algorithm, is a two-step classifier that assigns mgCSTs to vaginal metagenomes, providing standardized, scalable classifications.
papers.summary: VISTA is a new two-step classifier that assigns metagenomic community state types (mgCSTs) to vaginal microbiome samples, capturing within-species genetic and functional diversity. It provides standardized, scalable classification that links microbiome composition and function to health-related risk.

papers.title: Why Do We Lose Bone During Weight Loss: Can It Be Prevented?
papers.abstract: Weight loss is recommended for obesity management, but it also increases bone turnover and reduces bone mineral density (BMD) and bone quality (microarchitecture, geometry, and strength). This review examines mechanisms and the multiple factors that influence skeletal responses to caloric restriction.
papers.summary: This review examines why weight loss, though recommended for obesity management, leads to increased bone turnover and reduced bone mineral density, microarchitecture, geometry, and strength. It surveys the mechanisms and multiple factors that shape how the skeleton responds to caloric restriction, and discusses whether bone loss can be prevented.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics profiling of insomnia-related molecular features reveals microbiome, immune, and therapy-relevant heterogeneity in colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Emerging evidence implicates insomnia as a potential risk factor in carcinogenesis, potentially involving systemic inflammation, circadian disruption, and microbiome alterations. However, the molecular associations linking insomnia-related features to colorectal cancer (CRC), particularly with respect to tumor biology, immune microenvironmental states, and therapy-relevant phenotypes, remain largely unexplored. Multi-omics integration of genomic, transcriptomic, and microbiome data from 3,026 CRC patients across seven independent cohorts, including a large, well-annotated Clinical Omics study
papers.summary: This study integrates genomic, transcriptomic, and microbiome data from 3,026 colorectal cancer patients across seven cohorts to characterize molecular features associated with insomnia. The authors identify insomnia-related signatures linked to immune microenvironment states, microbiome composition, and therapy-relevant phenotypes, revealing substantial heterogeneity among CRC patients. These findings suggest insomnia-related molecular features may have clinical implications for CRC stratification and treatment.

papers.title: Real-time volatilomics reveals microbiota and pathogen fingerprints in the honey bee.
papers.abstract: Understanding the complex relationship between gut microbiota and their hosts often relies on invasive sampling techniques. Honey bees provide a tractable model for host-microbe studies. Here, we establish single-bee volatilomics using secondary electrospray ionization-high-resolution mass spectrometry (SESI-HRMS) to examine volatile organic compounds released to the air around an individual live honey bee. Specifically, we focused on the primary gut microbiota metabolites present in gnotobiotic bees. Our findings reveal distinct volatilome profiles in honey bees that depend on their gut bacte
papers.summary: This study establishes a real-time, non-invasive method called single-bee volatilomics using SESI-HRMS to detect volatile organic compounds emitted by individual live honey bees. The authors show that the volatile profiles differ depending on the bee's gut bacterial composition, allowing them to fingerprint both microbiota and pathogens without invasive sampling. This provides a new tool for studying host-microbe interactions in a tractable model organism.

papers.title: Phylogenomics of Desulfuromonadia supports reclassification of Geobacter psychrophilus as Irobacter psychrophilus comb. nov. and proposal of Geosyntrophus gen. nov.
papers.abstract: Genome-resolved phylogenomics reveals widespread misclassification of metal-reducing bacteria historically assigned to Geobacter based on 16S rRNA gene phylogeny, and highlights species that persist only as 16S rRNA entries without genomes for robust taxonomic resolution. Here, we resolve two such lineages by integrating whole-genome phylogeny with average amino acid identity (AAI) and percentage of conserved proteins (POCP) across 418 dereplicated genomes of Desulfuromonadia. We report a draft genome of the psychrophilic iron-reducing bacterium Geobacter psychrophilus (100% completeness). Phy
papers.summary: This study uses genome-resolved phylogenomics across 418 Desulfuromonadia genomes to show that many metal-reducing bacteria historically classified as Geobacter based on 16S rRNA are actually misclassified. The authors provide a complete draft genome for the psychrophilic iron-reducer Geobacter psychrophilus and, using whole-genome phylogeny plus AAI and POCP metrics, reclassify it as Irobacter psychrophilus comb. nov. and propose a new genus, Geosyntrophus.

papers.title: Wastewater-derived gut microbiome: global patterns and associations with population health.
papers.abstract: Urban wastewater systems aggregate gut microbiome signals from large populations, enabling exploration of their associations with population-level health patterns. However, it remains unclear whether wastewater-derived gut microbiome (WGM) simply represents a composite of individual gut microbes or whether it forms structured ecological patterns with potential relevance to population-level health-burden gradients. We analyzed 661 untreated wastewater metagenomes from 220 cities across 97 countries spanning all inhabited continents to characterize the global WGM. WGM exhibited broad phylogeneti
papers.summary: This study analyzed 661 untreated wastewater metagenomes from 220 cities across 97 countries to characterize global patterns in the wastewater-derived gut microbiome (WGM). The authors found that WGM exhibits structured ecological patterns rather than simply reflecting a composite of individual gut microbes, and these patterns associate with population-level health-burden gradients. The work establishes wastewater surveillance as a scalable tool for population health monitoring.

papers.title: Genome-resolved analysis reveals disruption of gut microbial vitamin B and K2 biosynthesis during Toxoplasma gondii infection in mice.
papers.abstract: Toxoplasma gondii infection remodels the gut microbiome, yet its impact on microbial vitamin biosynthetic potential and host redox metabolism remains unclear. Here, we integrated mouse gut metagenomes with publicly available metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) to construct a genome-resolved atlas of B-vitamin and vitamin K2 biosynthesis. From 45,697 MAGs, we curated 4,771 representative genomes, of which 2,682 met high-quality criteria (completeness ≥90%, contamination <5%). Functional annotation identified 229,717 vitamin-related genes corresponding to 177 Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Geno
papers.summary: This study used genome-resolved metagenomics to build an atlas of microbial B-vitamin and vitamin K2 biosynthesis pathways in the mouse gut, drawing on 45,697 metagenome-assembled genomes. Comparing infected and uninfected mice, the authors found that Toxoplasma gondii infection disrupts the gut microbiome's capacity to synthesize these vitamins, which may contribute to altered host redox metabolism. The work links a parasitic infection to functional shifts in microbial vitamin production.

papers.title: Performance Profiles of Short DNA Barcode Segments for Family Level Detection of Asteraceae Within Asterales.
papers.abstract: Short DNA barcodes may facilitate sequence recovery from degraded material, but their ability to retain target-family identity while excluding related taxa varies among genomic regions. We computationally evaluated 16 nuclear, plastid, and mitochondrial marker regions from 11 Asterales families using 279,956 NCBI locus-record matches and an accession-disjoint discovery/test design. Thirty-one candidate segments of 50-200 bp (mean, 98.55 bp) were screened in discovery data and evaluated for within-Asteraceae sequence recall, differentiation from non-Asteraceae Asterales, in silico primer behavi
papers.summary: This study computationally evaluated 16 nuclear, plastid, and mitochondrial DNA marker regions to identify short barcode segments (50-200 bp) that can reliably identify the plant family Asteraceae while excluding related families within Asterales. Using nearly 280,000 NCBI records with a discovery/test split, they screened 31 candidate segments for within-family recall, differentiation from non-Asteraceae taxa, and primer behavior. The work provides a systematic performance profile of short barcodes for family-level detection, useful where degraded DNA limits full-length barcoding.

papers.title: ON-Time enables rapid microbiome sequencing and analysis for precision medicine.
papers.abstract: Clinical application of microbiome-guided therapies in the intensive care unit (ICU) requires a method to rapidly analyze patient microbiomes to guide urgent treatment decisions. Conventional microbiome sequencing and analysis methods require long turnaround times, methodological complexity, and high costs that are barriers to clinical application. Here, we describe a method for rapid (<5 h turnaround from sample to results) and accurate metagenomic sequencing and taxonomic analysis of microbiomes in individual patient fecal samples, called ON-Time. ON-Time uses a simplified and rapid wet-lab
papers.summary: ON-Time is a new method for rapid metagenomic sequencing and taxonomic analysis of patient fecal microbiomes, achieving sample-to-results turnaround in under 5 hours. It addresses the long turnaround times, complexity, and high costs that have limited clinical microbiome-guided therapies, particularly in ICU settings. The approach aims to make microbiome profiling practical for urgent precision medicine decisions.

papers.title: Do Multi-Omics Approaches Improve the Diagnosis of Microbial Overgrowth Syndromes?
papers.abstract: This review investigates how advances in breath testing (BT), small bowel (SB) culture, metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, transcriptomics and proteomics are reshaping the definition and diagnosis of small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO). It also discusses whether SIBO should be redefined as part of a larger group of microbial overgrowth syndromes.
papers.summary: This review examines how emerging multi-omics technologies—including breath testing, small bowel culture, metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics—are reshaping the definition and diagnosis of small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO). It argues for potentially redefining SIBO as part of a broader category of microbial overgrowth syndromes, highlighting the limitations of current diagnostic approaches.

papers.title: Physiological Mechanisms of Silicon-Induced Drought Tolerance in Crops.
papers.abstract: Drought is one of the most damaging abiotic stresses affecting global crop productivity, and its frequency and severity are projected to increase under ongoing climate change. Silicon (Si), although not classified as an essential nutrient, is increasingly regarded as a "quasi-essential" beneficial element that improves crop performance under water-limited conditions. This review summarises the physiological mechanisms of Si-induced drought tolerance, based mainly on literature published in the past five years. Rather than presenting these mechanisms as an inventory of separate physiological ef
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent literature on how silicon application helps crops tolerate drought, focusing on physiological mechanisms rather than listing effects in isolation. It positions silicon as a quasi-essential beneficial element that improves crop performance under water-limited conditions, which are expected to worsen with climate change.

papers.title: Large-scale benchmarking of prokaryotic annotation tools across thousands of species.
papers.abstract: Genome annotation is an important step in deriving functional meaning from prokaryotic sequencing data, yet systematic evaluations guiding tool selection are lacking. We present the first large-scale investigation of four prominent open-source annotation tools (Prokka, Bakta, EggNOG-mapper, and PGAP) across 156,033 diverse genomes. This includes Escherichia coli strains for baseline performance, thousands of archaea and bacteria genomes, as well as frameshifted and metagenome-assembled genomes.
papers.summary: This study benchmarks four widely used prokaryotic genome annotation tools (Prokka, Bakta, EggNOG-mapper, and PGAP) across an unprecedented 156,033 diverse genomes, including E. coli, archaea, bacteria, and challenging frameshifted or metagenome-assembled genomes. It provides the first systematic, large-scale comparison to guide tool selection for functional annotation of prokaryotic sequencing data.

papers.title: Meta-CD: a metagenomic sequencing coverage and depth calculator for target species.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic Coverage and Depth Calculator (Meta-CD) is a convenient, biologist-friendly tool for determining coverage and depth to enhance taxonomic detection, functional profiling, and metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) recovery in metagenomics. It supports experimental design and post-sequencing analysis, modeling how genome size, relative abundance, sequencing depth, and DNA quantity influence detection of target species.
papers.summary: Meta-CD is a new user-friendly tool that calculates sequencing coverage and depth for target species in metagenomic samples. It models how factors like genome size, relative abundance, sequencing depth, and DNA input quantity affect the detection of specific organisms, helping researchers design experiments and interpret results.

papers.title: Targeting Stress and the Gut-Brain Axis: Effects of Lifestyle and Psychobiotic Interventions on the Gut Microbiome in Adults-A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Stress is increasingly recognized as an important modulator of gut microbiome composition and function through the bidirectional microbiota-gut-brain axis. Dietary, psychobiotic, and other lifestyle-oriented interventions have therefore attracted growing interest as potential strategies for simultaneously influencing stress-related outcomes and the gut microbiome. This systematic review aimed to evaluate randomized controlled trials (RCTs) investigating the effects of lifestyle-oriented and psychobiotic interventions on both stress-related outcomes and the gut microbiome
papers.summary: This systematic review evaluates randomized controlled trials testing whether lifestyle-oriented and psychobiotic interventions (such as probiotics and dietary changes) can simultaneously improve stress-related outcomes and alter gut microbiome composition in adults. It synthesizes evidence on the microbiota-gut-brain axis as a target for stress management, though the abstract provides limited detail on the specific findings or effect sizes.

papers.title: Impact of Feed Intake and Body Fat Deposition on Reproductive Performance and Placental Function of Shaziling Sows: A Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: Excessive body fat deposition during pregnancy is believed to have an adverse effect on the reproductive performance of sows. Feed intake regulation (REG) is an effective method to modulate energy intake and fat deposition. This study aimed to explore the impact of feed intake and body fat deposition on reproductive performance. A total of 24 Shaziling sows (parity 3-6) were divided into two groups based on their BF on day 30 of gestation, and subsequently randomly assigned to control (CON) and REG groups: (1) BF between 12 and 16 mm (LB-CON, n = 6), (2) BF between 12 and 16 mm (LB-IF, n = 6),
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This pilot study examined how feed intake regulation affects body fat deposition and reproductive outcomes in Shaziling sows, a Chinese native breed. Sows were grouped by backfat thickness at day 30 of gestation and assigned to control or regulated feeding regimens to assess impacts on reproductive performance and placental function. The work provides preliminary evidence linking feed intake management to fat deposition and placental physiology in this breed.

papers.title: Spatially Specialized Nasopharynx-Rectal Microbiomes in Golden Snub-Nosed Monkeys (Rhinopithecus roxellana).
papers.abstract: Understanding the nasopharyngeal (NAS) and rectal (INT) microbiomes is critical to maintain host health. However, their functional roles in shaping microbial network structure and niche differentiation remain unexplored in most animal species, especially endangered primates. Here, we compared the NAS and INT microbiomes of golden snub-nosed monkeys (Rhinopithecus roxellana) using full-length 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing and metagenomics, focusing on taxonomic composition, functional profiles (KEGG, CAZy, PHI), and microbial co-occurrence networks.
papers.summary: This study compares the nasopharyngeal and rectal microbiomes of endangered golden snub-nosed monkeys using full-length 16S rRNA sequencing and metagenomics, examining taxonomic composition, functional profiles (KEGG, CAZy, PHI), and microbial co-occurrence networks. The authors find that these two body sites harbor spatially specialized microbial communities with distinct functional capacities and network structures, highlighting niche differentiation within the host microbiome.

papers.title: The cystic fibrosis gut microbial dysbiosis index (CF-GMDI): a quantitative measure of gut microbial imbalance in children with cystic fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Gut dysbiosis is a hallmark of cystic fibrosis (CF), typically characterised using non-specific diversity metrics and study-specific taxonomic lists, limiting comparability across studies. We aimed to develop a metagenomic, species-level CF Gut Microbial Dysbiosis Index (CF-GMDI) to standardise measurement of gut microbial imbalance in children with CF (cwCF) METHODS: CF-GMDI was derived using stool metagenomic data from the PEARL-CF study (70 cwCF; 67 healthy controls (HC); 0-6 years). Differentially abundant taxa were identified between cwCF and HC using MaAsLin2. The index was calculated as
papers.journal: Journal of cystic fibrosis : official journal of the European Cystic Fibrosis Society
papers.summary: This study introduces the CF-GMDI, a metagenomic species-level index that quantifies gut microbial dysbiosis in children with cystic fibrosis using stool samples from the PEARL-CF cohort. By identifying differentially abundant taxa between CF and healthy controls, the index provides a standardized, quantitative measure that improves comparability across studies.

papers.title: Optimizing a culture-enriched hybrid metagenomics pipeline to assess the AMR footprint of livestock manure in anaerobic digestate.
papers.abstract: The role of environmental samples from livestock production systems, including manure and anaerobic digestate, as reservoirs of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) is likely underestimated because conventional metagenomic approaches can overlook low-abundance ARGs and often lack the resolution to associate these genes with their microbial hosts and co-localized mobile genetic elements (MGEs). We evaluated whether culture-enriched metagenomics (CEMG), with and without antibiotic selection, enhances ARG detection in anaerobic digestate and improves the resolution of ARG-MGE-host associations u
papers.summary: This study evaluates a culture-enriched hybrid metagenomics pipeline to better detect antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) in livestock manure and anaerobic digestate, which conventional metagenomics often misses due to low abundance. By adding culture enrichment with and without antibiotic selection, the authors improve detection of ARGs and their associations with microbial hosts and mobile genetic elements. The work offers an optimized approach for monitoring the environmental AMR footprint of agricultural waste.

papers.title: Two Bacillus PGPB Strains in Wheat and Soybean: Wheat Growth Promotion Without Detectable Rhizosphere Microbiome Restructuring.
papers.abstract: Plant growth-promoting bacteria (PGPB) are increasingly deployed as biofertilizers, yet the link between an inoculant's genomic potential and its realized effect on the plant is rarely assessed within an integrative framework that jointly captures the rhizosphere microbiome, plant phenotype, and strain genome. Two Bacillus strains-B. halotolerans 1453 and B. pumilus 630-were applied to wheat and soybean in a factorial pot experiment (2 strains × 2 application methods × 3 frequencies + control, 3-4 replicates). Rhizosphere samples (n = 67 after filtering) were profiled by 16S rRNA sequencing wi
papers.summary: This study tested two Bacillus plant growth-promoting bacterial strains on wheat and soybean in a controlled pot experiment, combining 16S rRNA rhizosphere profiling with plant phenotyping and genomic analysis. The strains promoted wheat growth but did not detectably restructure the rhizosphere microbiome, highlighting a disconnect between an inoculant's genomic potential and its realized ecological impact. The integrative framework shows that growth promotion can occur without major microbiome shifts.

papers.title: Effects of Dietary Glucose, Fructose, and Monosaccharide-to-Lard Energy Ratios on Cecal Microbiota Composition and Ecological Organization in Rats.
papers.abstract: Background: Although dietary fat and carbohydrates are major determinants of gut microbiota composition, their interactive effects across changing dietary monosaccharide-to-lard energy ratios remain incompletely understood. This study descriptively examined treatment-level cecal microbiome profiles across dietary gradients in which lard (L) was progressively replaced with glucose (G) or fructose (F). Methods: A carbohydrate-free, lard-rich control diet was formulated, and lard was progressively replaced with glucose or fructose while maintaining a constant protein-to-energy ratio. Cecal conten
papers.summary: This study examined how progressively replacing dietary lard with glucose or fructose affects cecal microbiota composition and ecological organization in rats. The authors found that the type of monosaccharide and the monosaccharide-to-fat energy ratio both shape microbiome structure, with distinct community-level responses to glucose versus fructose gradients.

papers.title: Identifying fundamental gaps in functional metagenomics: a step towards unlocking microbiome research potential.
papers.abstract: Incomplete functional annotation limits biological interpretation in microbiome studies and their translational potential. Poor annotation arises from multiple causes, with incomplete gene-protein-reaction mapping being one tractable yet under-examined contributor. We address this gap by developing a comprehensive hierarchical framework that systematically integrates gene families in UniRef, proteins in UniProt, and metabolic reactions in MetaCyc and BioCyc through UniProtKB accession, EC number, and Pfam-domain matching. Applied to a human gut metagenome dataset via HUMAnN3, our MetaCyc-based
papers.summary: This paper develops a hierarchical framework that links gene families (UniRef), proteins (UniProt), and metabolic reactions (MetaCyc/BioCyc) using UniProtKB accessions, EC numbers, and Pfam domains to improve functional annotation in metagenomics. Applied to human gut metagenome data via HUMAnN3, it identifies gaps in gene-protein-reaction mapping that limit biological interpretation of microbiome studies. The work highlights a tractable contributor to poor annotation and offers a step toward unlocking microbiome research potential.

papers.title: Lifestyle Impacts the Oral Microbiome of Classical and Post-Classical Societies in Italy.
papers.abstract: The fall of the Roman Empire (476 CE) profoundly affected the lives of its peoples due to the political, administrative, and territorial changes that occurred. The majority of written records of the time focus on the social élite, leaving larger parts of the population understudied. Here, we employ a bioarchaeological approach to understand how differences in lifestyle may be reflected in the oral microbiome of people from different social classes living before and after the fall.
papers.summary: This study uses bioarchaeological analysis of ancient dental calculus to compare the oral microbiomes of individuals from different social classes before and after the fall of the Roman Empire in Italy. The authors find that lifestyle differences, including social class and the political upheaval following 476 CE, are reflected in the composition of the oral microbiome. The work demonstrates the utility of ancient oral microbiome analysis for studying how historical social and political changes affected the health and daily lives of non-elite populations.

papers.title: Assembly Dynamics and Functional Divergence of Anaerobic Communities Driven by Iron Oxides.
papers.abstract: Iron oxides play an important role in regulating global biogeochemical cycles, yet how their physicochemical properties influence community structure, function, and assembly remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the effects of four representative iron oxides-ferrihydrite (Fh), goethite (Gt), haematite (Ht), and magnetite (Mt)-serving as terminal electron acceptors on microbial communities enriched from activated sludge. Metagenomic profiling revealed mineral-dependent divergence in community composition and functional potential. The communities developed on amorphous Fh demonstrated
papers.summary: This study shows that different iron oxide minerals (ferrihydrite, goethite, haematite, magnetite) acting as terminal electron acceptors drive distinct microbial community compositions and functional potentials in anaerobic enrichments from activated sludge. Metagenomic profiling revealed mineral-dependent divergence, with amorphous ferrihydrite supporting a notably different community than the more crystalline minerals.

papers.title: Convergent methodologies in prosthetic joint infection research: integrating transdisciplinary approaches to understand and prevent biofilm-driven failure of orthopaedic prostheses.
papers.abstract: Prosthetic joint infections (PJIs) remain among the most devastating complications of arthroplasty, imposing substantial clinical, economic and patient burdens. Although culture-based diagnostics underpin current clinical practice, PJIs are biofilm-driven infections shaped by taxonomic diversity, spatial organization, host responses and surface interactions, meaning conventional approaches provide only a partial and often decontextualized view of the infection process. We examine how convergent methodologies can transform PJI research by integrating approaches that have traditionally been stud
papers.summary: This review argues that prosthetic joint infections (PJIs) are biofilm-driven processes that culture-based diagnostics fail to capture fully, and that integrating transdisciplinary methods—such as advanced imaging, multi-omics, and spatial analyses—is needed to understand and prevent implant failure. It surveys how convergent methodologies can provide a more contextualized view of the taxonomic diversity, spatial organization, and host-surface interactions underlying PJIs.

papers.title: Benchmarking methods for extracting microbial signal from host-dominated metatranscriptomes.
papers.abstract: Human RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data originally generated for human transcriptome profiling are overwhelmingly dominated by host sequences, yet they often contain a small fraction of non-human reads that can be exploited for microbial detection. When such datasets are repurposed for secondary microbiome-oriented analyses, extracting and accurately classifying this weak microbial signal becomes technically challenging, and no ready-to-use pipeline currently exists. In this study, we evaluate computational strategies for filtering host reads and classifying microbial transcripts in host-dominated
papers.summary: This study benchmarks computational strategies for extracting and classifying the weak microbial signal present in host-dominated RNA-seq datasets originally generated for human transcriptome profiling. The authors evaluate host-read filtering and microbial transcript classification approaches, addressing the lack of a ready-to-use pipeline for repurposing such data in secondary microbiome analyses.

papers.title: Major Depressive Disorder Signatures: A Review of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Powered Insights Into Gut Dysbiosis.
papers.abstract: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is a highly common neuropsychiatric disorder globally. A variety of factors contribute to the neuropathology of MDD. Microbiome research in neuropsychiatric disorders such as MDD has recently attracted attention. Indeed, the gut-brain axis could influence the course of MDD through metabolites such as Gamma-Aminobutyric Acid (GABA), Quinolinate, and other factors. Such metabolites may modulate the balance of excitatory and inhibitory signals. Moreover, MDD features abundant hyperinflammatory bacteria, whereas anti-inflammatory butyrate-synthesizing genera are dec
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence approaches are being applied to understand gut microbiome dysbiosis in major depressive disorder. It highlights the gut-brain axis and specific microbial metabolites like GABA and quinolinate that may influence excitatory/inhibitory signaling, alongside shifts toward hyperinflammatory bacteria and reduced butyrate-producing genera in MDD patients.

papers.title: Evaluation of a Lactobacillus biopreservative on milk cake quality: Effects on physicochemical, microbiological, and flavor properties.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the effectiveness of preservation films derived from two Lactobacillus biopreservatives in maintaining the freshness of milk cake. The biopreservatives, fermented whey and its cell-free supernatant (CFS), were produced synergistically by high-exopolysaccharide (EPS)-producing Limosilactobacillus fermentum A51 and high-phenyllactic acid (PLA)-producing Lactobacillus plantarum L3. Both biopreservatives, rich in EPS (412.91-429.33 mg/L) and PLA (69.24-70.55 mg/L), showed strong antioxidant and antibacterial activity. EPS formed a stable protective film on milk cake surface
papers.summary: This study developed preservation films from two Lactobacillus biopreservatives (fermented whey and its cell-free supernatant) produced by high-EPS Limosilactobacillus fermentum A51 and high-PLA Lactobacillus plantarum L3. The biopreservatives were rich in exopolysaccharides and phenyllactic acid, showed strong antioxidant and antibacterial activity, and formed a protective film that maintained milk cake freshness. The work demonstrates a natural, biopreservative-based approach to extend the shelf life of dairy products.

papers.title: Immune regulatory networks and gut microbiota-associated targets in endometriosis: an integrative multi-omics and network analysis.
papers.abstract: Endometriosis is an estrogen-dependent disorder characterized by chronic inflammation, immune dysregulation, and altered hormone metabolism. Although gut microbiota-derived metabolites have been implicated in shaping immune microenvironments and lesion development, the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated multi-omics, protein-protein interaction (PPI), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and single-cell transcriptomics to identify core targets and delineate their interactions with microbiota-derived metabolites, followed by molecular simulation
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics, protein-protein interaction networks, SHAP-based machine learning interpretation, and single-cell transcriptomics to identify core immune-regulatory targets in endometriosis and link them to gut microbiota-derived metabolites. The authors propose candidate molecular targets and regulatory interactions that may connect the gut microbiome to endometriosis-associated immune dysregulation.

papers.title: Metagenome-scale modeling to assess microbiome metabolic complementarity for precision microbiota transplantation therapies.
papers.abstract: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) holds therapeutic promise beyond recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection, but clinical outcomes remain unpredictable and donor-selection strategies remain limited, in part because the role of donor‒recipient metabolic interactions in shaping the post-FMT community remains poorly understood. Here, we leverage metagenome-scale metabolic modeling to quantify metabolic niche complementarity between donor and recipient microbiomes and predict post-FMT community composition. Using MICOM-derived metabolic models, we show that donor genomes whose metabolic f
papers.summary: This study uses metagenome-scale metabolic modeling (MICOM) to quantify metabolic niche complementarity between donor and recipient microbiomes, aiming to predict post-FMT community composition and improve donor selection. The authors show that donor genomes whose metabolic capabilities complement the recipient's existing community better predict engraftment outcomes, offering a framework for precision microbiota transplantation.

papers.title: Integrated metagenomic and metabolomic analysis identifies severity-specific inflammatory and metabolic signatures in post-stroke depression.
papers.abstract: Post-stroke depression (PSD) is a common complication that significantly impacts patient prognosis. This study aimed to systematically characterize the associations among gut microbial ecology, metabolic profiles, and inflammatory responses across different severities of PSD. We conducted metagenomic sequencing, non-targeted metabolomics, and serum cytokine analysis (IL-1β, IL-6, IL-10, IL-18, TNF-α, IFN-γ, and CRP) in 91 patients with varying degrees of PSD and non-PSD controls. Bioinformatics analyzes were employed to construct multi-omics association networks and machine learning models. Re
papers.summary: This study combined gut metagenomics, serum metabolomics, and cytokine profiling in 91 stroke patients to characterize how gut microbial ecology, metabolic profiles, and inflammation differ across post-stroke depression (PSD) severities. Multi-omics network analysis and machine learning identified severity-specific microbial, metabolic, and inflammatory signatures that distinguish PSD grades from non-PSD controls.

papers.title: GUTchetp: integrated prediction of gut microbial biotransformation profiles using ensemble monolingual and multilingual neural machine translation and enzyme class consistency-reaction similarity.
papers.abstract: The analysis of the metabolic fate of chemical compounds in the human gut remains a fundamental challenge, as comprehensive experimental characterization across the vast chemical space is infeasible. Moreover, despite progress in computational biology, a comprehensive tool for predicting microbe-dependent metabolism of diverse chemicals is still lacking. To address these challenges, we introduce the GUTchetp framework, which comprises two components: one predicts gut biotransformation products and was tested on a benchmark of six compound categories, whereas the other identifies the associated
papers.summary: GUTchetp is a new computational framework that predicts how gut microbes chemically transform diverse compounds, using an ensemble of monolingual and multilingual neural machine translation models combined with enzyme class consistency and reaction similarity. It was benchmarked across six compound categories and also identifies the enzymes responsible for the predicted biotransformations. The tool addresses the lack of comprehensive computational methods for predicting microbe-dependent metabolism in the human gut.

papers.title: Towards optimizing the host response to biotics: a report of an International Scientific Association for Probiotics and Prebiotics working group.
papers.abstract: This report summarizes the deliberations of a working group convened by the International Scientific Association for Probiotics and Prebiotics (ISAPP) at their 2025 annual meeting to identify the key targets that mediate the host response to biotics. Probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics, and postbiotics have been explored in numerous contexts, but results of clinical trials are mixed. In most studies performed to date, a therapeutic product and its dose and administration strategy were selected based on factors other than rigorous mechanistic evidence. Given recent advances in our understanding
papers.summary: This report summarizes an ISAPP working group's effort to identify the key host targets that mediate responses to probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics, and postbiotics. The authors argue that clinical trials of these biotics have yielded mixed results largely because product, dose, and administration choices have not been guided by rigorous mechanistic evidence. The report aims to set a framework for optimizing host responses to biotics based on mechanistic understanding.

papers.title: Probiotics in asthma: immunoregulatory mechanisms and emerging opportunities for respiratory delivery-a narrative review.
papers.abstract: Asthma is a complex heterogeneous respiratory disease influenced by various factors such as genetics, immunity, and environment. Probiotics and related microbial preparations can be used in the prevention and treatment of asthma. This review aims to clarify the role and mechanism of microbial preparations in the treatment of asthma through respiratory administration, as well as the theoretical basis as delivery carriers. This may provide new insights for the prevention and treatment of asthma.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines how probiotics and microbial preparations delivered via the respiratory route may prevent and treat asthma through immunoregulatory mechanisms. It discusses the theoretical basis for using microbes as delivery carriers and highlights emerging opportunities for respiratory administration. The review synthesizes existing evidence to propose new directions for asthma prevention and treatment.

papers.title: Distinctive Patterns of Gut Bifidobacterium Diversity in Mongolian Adults: Regional Variation and Dairy Intake Associations.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Despite increasing interest in the human gut microbiome, particularly in Bifidobacterium, studies focusing on traditionally living populations with high habitual dairy consumption remain limited. This study investigated species-level diversity, abundance, and regional variation of Bifidobacterium among healthy Mongolian adults and contextualized these findings within a global comparative framework. Methods: A total of 100 healthy adults were recruited from four Mongolian regions. Fecal samples were analyzed using species-resolved shotgun metagenomics, and dietary intake
papers.summary: This study used species-resolved shotgun metagenomics to profile gut Bifidobacterium diversity in 100 healthy Mongolian adults across four regions, finding distinctive patterns linked to regional variation and habitual dairy consumption. The findings are contextualized within a global comparative framework, highlighting how traditional diets shape microbiome composition in understudied populations.

papers.title: Non-Thermal Plasma-Mediated Redox Signaling and Microbiome Interactions for Abiotic Stress Adaptation: Molecular Insights and Future Prospects for Sustainable Agriculture.
papers.abstract: Crop production is continually exposed to a wide range of abiotic stresses that negatively affect growth and yield, posing a severe threat to global food security. Plant growth-promoting bacteria (PGPB) promote nutrient assimilation, activate antioxidant enzymes, and stimulate phytohormone production to mitigate abiotic stress. However, the effective application of PGPB in the field depends on host colonization, soil specificity, and susceptibility to competitive microbial communities. Recently, non-thermal plasma (NTP) has emerged as a revolutionary tool for sustainable agriculture, making it
papers.summary: This review examines how non-thermal plasma (NTP) can be combined with plant growth-promoting bacteria (PGPB) to help crops tolerate abiotic stresses such as drought, salinity, and heat. It discusses the molecular mechanisms—including redox signaling and microbiome interactions—through which NTP may enhance PGPB colonization and effectiveness in the field, while outlining challenges and future research directions for sustainable agriculture.

papers.title: From Phytochemical Diversity to Clinical Translation: Preparation-Dependent Bioactivity of Echinacea purpurea.
papers.abstract: Preparations of Echinacea purpurea vary in biological effects according to plant organ, cultivation conditions, extraction procedure, and phytochemical profile. This structured critical narrative review integrates analytical, preclinical, and clinical evidence on the phytochemical diversity and preparation-dependent activities of E. purpurea, with particular emphasis on caffeic acid derivatives, alkamides, polysaccharides, flavonoids, and volatile constituents. The literature published from January 2000 to July 2026 was evaluated across chemical, computational, cellular, animal, and human stud
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence showing that the biological effects of Echinacea purpurea preparations depend heavily on plant organ, cultivation conditions, extraction methods, and resulting phytochemical profiles, with key compounds including caffeic acid derivatives, alkamides, polysaccharides, flavonoids, and volatiles. It integrates analytical, preclinical, and clinical literature from 2000 to 2026 to highlight how this variability complicates clinical translation and reproducibility.

papers.title: Metagenomic insights into mechanisms of coral larval settlement induction and inhibition by marine biofilms.
papers.abstract: Biofilms are essential to larval settlement in many marine invertebrates, yet the mechanisms driving settlement induction or inhibition in corals remain poorly resolved. This challenge lies in the vast taxonomic and functional diversity of marine biofilms, making it difficult to identify cues associated with settlement. To address this, we analysed the metagenomes of biofilms used to induce settlement (attachment and metamorphosis) of four broadcast-spawning non-acroporid coral species: Dipsastrea favus, Platygyra sinensis, Echinophyllia aspera and Porites lobata. Biofilms were developed for o
papers.summary: This study used metagenomic sequencing of marine biofilms to identify the microbial taxa and functional genes associated with inducing or inhibiting larval settlement in four non-acroporid coral species. By comparing biofilms that promote attachment and metamorphosis versus those that do not, the authors pinpointed specific microbial metabolic pathways and cues likely responsible for settlement outcomes. The findings offer new mechanistic insight into how biofilm composition shapes coral recruitment, with potential implications for reef restoration.

papers.title: Exploring the ecological drivers of bacteriophage diversity and functional viral potential in the skin of the axolotl Ambystoma altamirani.
papers.abstract: Bacteriophages play important roles in shaping microbial community dynamics across diverse environments. In the amphibian skin, most microbiome studies have focused on bacteria and their interactions with the fungus Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd), leaving other microbial components, including viruses, largely unexplored. Here, we present the first characterization of the viral community in the amphibian skin microbiome, focusing on ecological drivers of bacteriophage diversity and functional potential in the axolotl Ambystoma altamirani. Using public shotgun metagenomes, we found that the
papers.summary: This study provides the first characterization of the viral community (bacteriophages) in amphibian skin microbiomes, using public shotgun metagenomes from the axolotl Ambystoma altamirani. It explores ecological drivers of phage diversity and functional potential, expanding beyond the typical bacterial-focused amphibian microbiome research.

papers.title: The chromosomal genome sequence of a staghorn coral, Acropora cf.  manni (Scleractinia: Acroporidae).
papers.abstract: We present a genome assembly from a colony sample of Acropora cf. manni (staghorn coral; Cnidaria; Anthozoa; Scleractinia; Acroporidae). The assembly contains two haplotypes with total lengths of 459.26 megabases and 489.30 megabases. Most of haplotype 1 (94.39%) is scaffolded into 14 chromosomal pseudomolecules. Haplotype 2 was assembled to scaffold level. The mitochondrial genome has also been assembled, with a length of 18.48 kilobases. Metagenome binning recovered one bacterial bin from the phylum Chlamydiota.
papers.summary: This paper reports a high-quality chromosome-level genome assembly for the staghorn coral Acropora cf. manni, with two haplotypes of roughly 459 and 489 megabases, most of haplotype 1 scaffolded into 14 chromosomes. The mitochondrial genome was also assembled, and a bacterial symbiont genome from the phylum Chlamydiota was recovered via metagenome binning. This adds a valuable reference genome for coral reef research.

papers.title: Gut microbiota dynamics and metabolic pathways associated with bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis progression.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a progressive respiratory disease characterized by epithelial injury, aberrant repair and excessive extracellular matrix deposition. Although the gut-lung axis is increasingly implicated in respiratory disorders, stage-resolved characterization of gut microbiota taxonomic and functional potential during PF development is limited.
papers.summary: This study characterizes how gut microbiota composition and predicted metabolic functions change across stages of bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis in a mouse model. It links specific taxonomic shifts and metabolic pathways to disease progression, supporting the gut-lung axis hypothesis. The findings provide a stage-resolved framework for understanding microbial contributions to fibrosis.

papers.title: Short-read genome skimming enables molecular barcoding of old myxomycete collections.
papers.abstract: This study evaluates the effectiveness of Illumina-based genome skimming for barcoding myxomycete herbarium collections ranging from 29 to 91 years in age. We successfully retrieved partial sequences of the standard marker gene (nucSSU) in all cases, as well as additional markers (mtSSU, EF1a, and COI) for certain collections. Altogether, 28 genes were recognized in the studied material. In a 33-year-old specimen of Lindbladia tubulina, the assembly reached an N50 of 4.19 kb, enabling the recovery of extended functional loci. The input genomic DNA quantity emerges as the primary determinant of
papers.summary: This study shows that Illumina genome skimming can recover barcode and additional marker sequences from myxomycete herbarium specimens up to 91 years old, with the standard nucSSU marker retrieved in all samples. The amount of input genomic DNA was the main factor determining success, and one 33-year-old specimen yielded an assembly with an N50 of 4.19 kb, allowing recovery of extended functional loci.

papers.title: Metagenomic insights into antibiotic resistance genes and virulence factors in sediments of river Yamuna.
papers.abstract: Riverine sediments serve as critical reservoirs of microbial diversity and functional genes, reflecting both natural ecological processes and anthropogenic impacts. In the present study, we employed a shotgun metagenomic approach to investigate microbial community composition, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes, and virulence factors in sediments collected from three environmentally distinct locations of the Yamuna River near Agra, India, representing BSA, TGY, and YEA. The sediment DNA was subjected to high-throughput Illumina sequencing, followed by quality control, assembly, and open read
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics to profile microbial communities, antibiotic resistance genes, and virulence factors in sediments from three sites along the Yamuna River near Agra, India. The findings reveal how anthropogenic pollution shapes the resistome and virulome in riverine sediments, highlighting sediments as reservoirs for clinically relevant genes.

papers.title: A Pan-European Whole-Microbiome Study of Wastewater Influent: Prokaryotes, Protists, Fungi, and Metazoa.
papers.abstract: Microbial communities entering wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) through untreated sewage represent an important interface between human, environmental, and treatment-associated microbiomes, yet our understanding of their biogeography remains poorly resolved, particularly for microbial eukaryotes. Using shotgun metagenomic time-series data from influent samples of seven WWTPs across a European latitudinal gradient, we analyzed the taxonomic composition and dynamics of bacteria, protists, fungi, and microscopic metazoa. Influent community composition varied with geographic location and season
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic time-series data from seven wastewater treatment plants across a European latitudinal gradient to characterize the full microbiome of untreated sewage influent, including bacteria, protists, fungi, and microscopic metazoa. The authors found that influent community composition varied with both geographic location and season, providing a broad view of the biogeography of wastewater-associated microbial eukaryotes, which have been less studied than prokaryotes.

papers.title: Lesion-specific oral microbiome signatures and predicted carcinogenic pathways in oral squamous cell carcinoma: a paired-site study in Pakistan.
papers.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma accounts for over 90% of oral neoplasms. Despite therapeutic advances, the lack of reliable, non-invasive biomarkers and delayed diagnosis continues to impede effective clinical management. By combining paired lesion and non-lesion sampling with predictive metagenomics analysis, our study addresses this gap and advances the current understanding of microbiome‒tumor interactions.
papers.summary: This study compared the oral microbiome at tumor sites versus matched non-lesion sites in patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma in Pakistan, identifying lesion-specific bacterial signatures. Using predictive metagenomic analysis, the authors also inferred microbial pathways that may contribute to carcinogenesis, suggesting potential non-invasive biomarkers for early detection.

papers.title: Host identity dominates over intra-ruminal spatial variation in shaping the rumen microbiome of Holstein-Friesian dairy cows.
papers.abstract: The rumen is a structurally complex fermentation chamber with distinct physicochemical zones, resulting in intra-ruminal biogeography and raising the question whether microbial communities vary spatially within the rumen. We investigated the extent of intra-ruminal microbial variation by analyzing rumen fluid collected from six rumen cannulated Holstein-Friesian dairy cows. Rumen fluid samples were obtained in duplicate from three anatomical rumen regions: the cranial sac (Front), the front ventral sac (Middle), and the middle ventral sac (Back).and subjected to 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequenci
papers.summary: This study examined whether microbial communities differ across anatomical regions within the rumen of six cannulated Holstein-Friesian dairy cows by sampling rumen fluid from three locations and performing 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. The results show that host identity (which cow the sample came from) explains far more of the microbial community variation than the intra-ruminal sampling location, indicating that spatial biogeography within the rumen is relatively minor compared to individual host effects.

papers.title: A γ-polyglutamic acid-based artificial biofilm for field delivery of Bacillus amyloliquefaciens KNU-28: an uncontrolled multi-orchard demonstration on peach gummosis with exploratory bark fungal community profiling.
papers.abstract: Peach gummosis, caused primarily by Botryosphaeria dothidea sensu lato, is a destructive canker disease with few environmentally friendly management options. Here we report an uncontrolled pre/post field demonstration of a γ-polyglutamic acid-based artificial biofilm - a biodegradable delivery platform whose agent-agnostic design remains untested - encapsulating Bacillus amyloliquefaciens KNU-28 across 143 trees in 18 commercial peach orchards in South Korea. Severity declined from a pre-treatment mean of 4.12 (April) to 2.32 by August (76.2% of 143 trees improved by ≥1 point) and to 1.78 by O
papers.summary: This study tested a biodegradable γ-polyglutamic acid-based artificial biofilm encapsulating Bacillus amyloliquefaciens KNU-28 for delivering biocontrol bacteria to peach trees affected by gummosis across 18 commercial orchards. Disease severity dropped substantially from a pre-treatment mean of 4.12 to 1.78 by the end of the season, with 76.2% of trees improving by at least one point. The work also included exploratory profiling of bark fungal communities, though the uncontrolled design limits causal conclusions.

papers.title: Evaluation of a COX-2 fluorescent probe for adjunctive quantitative assessment of BV-associated inflammatory severity.
papers.abstract: Bacterial vaginosis (BV) is a prevalent lower genital tract infection linked to significant reproductive health complications. Current diagnostics are subjective or non-quantitative for clinical use. This study aims to evaluate a novel cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2)-targeting fluorescent probe as an adjunctive quantitative tool for assessing BV-associated inflammatory severity within a standard BV diagnostic workflow.
papers.summary: This study evaluates a fluorescent probe targeting COX-2, an inflammation-associated enzyme, as a potential adjunctive tool for quantitatively assessing inflammatory severity in bacterial vaginosis (BV). The goal is to complement standard BV diagnostics, which are currently subjective or non-quantitative, with an objective measure of inflammation.

papers.title: The metastatic spectrum in functional and non-functional NENs: mechanistic insights from multi-omics.
papers.abstract: Neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) are biologically heterogeneous tumors in which differentiation/grade and hormonal functionality are intersecting but non-equivalent axes. This review focuses on functional and non-functional well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), principally gastroenteropancreatic and pancreatic NETs, and critically evaluates how site, lineage, stage, tumor burden, genomic and epigenetic alterations, immune-stromal remodeling, metabolic adaptation, microbiome-associated signals, and treatment pressure converge on metastasis and recurrence. Apparent outcome differences
papers.summary: This review examines how functional and non-functional well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs), mainly gastroenteropancreatic and pancreatic, differ in their metastatic behavior. It synthesizes multi-omics evidence—genomic, epigenetic, immune-stromal, metabolic, and microbiome signals—to argue that differentiation/grade and hormonal functionality are intersecting but distinct axes shaping metastasis and recurrence. The authors critically evaluate how tumor site, lineage, stage, and treatment pressure converge on metastatic outcomes.

papers.title: Oral dysbiosis in children with renal failure: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: The oral microbiome plays an important role in maintaining host homeostasis and may interact with systemic diseases through the oral-systemic axis. Chronic kidney disease (CKD) in childhood is associated with chronic inflammation, metabolic alterations, and immune dysfunction, which may influence microbial ecosystems. While intestinal dysbiosis has been widely studied in paediatric CKD, alterations in the oral microbiome remain less well understood. The aim of this study was to qualitatively synthesize evidence on oral microbiome alterations in children and adolescents with CKD compared with s
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes evidence on oral microbiome alterations in children and adolescents with chronic kidney disease (CKD) compared to healthy controls. The findings suggest that pediatric CKD is associated with oral dysbiosis, though the evidence base remains limited and heterogeneous. The review highlights the oral-systemic axis as a potentially understudied dimension of CKD pathophysiology in children.

papers.title: Beyond antibiotics: artificial intelligence-enabled anti-infective ecosystems for next-generation precision therapeutics against antimicrobial resistance.
papers.abstract: The rapid global expansion of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) threatens to undermine decades of progress in infectious disease management and highlights the limitations of conventional antibiotic-centered therapeutic strategies. Although emerging technologies-including antimicrobial peptides, bacteriophage therapy, CRISPR-based antimicrobials, microbiome therapeutics, anti-virulence approaches, nanotechnology-enabled drug delivery, and artificial intelligence (AI)-have individually demonstrated considerable promise, they are predominantly being developed as independent interventions rather than
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This review argues that antimicrobial resistance (AMR) cannot be solved by conventional antibiotics alone, and that emerging alternatives such as antimicrobial peptides, phage therapy, CRISPR antimicrobials, microbiome therapeutics, anti-virulence strategies, and nanotech delivery should be integrated rather than developed in isolation. The authors propose an AI-enabled 'anti-infective ecosystem' framework to coordinate these diverse modalities for next-generation precision therapeutics.

papers.title: Integrative artificial intelligence and multi-omics modeling approach for characterizing microbial dynamics and health impacts in space microgravity and radiation conditions.
papers.abstract: Characterizing microbial dynamics and their potential health impacts under space microgravity and radiation conditions remains a major challenge in space biology. The complexity of microbial adaptation, host associated microbiome variation, and heterogeneous multi omics responses requires computational methods that can jointly model temporal dynamics, biological interactions, and predictive uncertainty.
papers.summary: This paper proposes an integrative AI and multi-omics modeling framework to characterize how microbial communities adapt and affect health under space microgravity and radiation conditions. The approach jointly models temporal dynamics, biological interactions, and predictive uncertainty to address the complexity of host-microbiome responses in spaceflight environments.

papers.title: Effects of electroacupuncture on neurological outcomes and brain-gut axis-associated changes in experimental ischemic stroke models: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of death and disability worldwide and is frequently accompanied by brain-gut axis disturbances, including intestinal barrier dysfunction, gut microbiota dysbiosis, and immune-inflammatory imbalance. Although electroacupuncture (EA) has demonstrated neuroprotective effects in experimental stroke, its effects on brain-gut axis-related outcomes have not been systematically evaluated.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates whether electroacupuncture improves neurological outcomes in experimental ischemic stroke models and whether these benefits are linked to brain-gut axis changes such as intestinal barrier function, gut microbiota composition, and immune-inflammatory balance. It synthesizes preclinical evidence to assess both neuroprotective effects and gut-related mechanisms.

papers.title: Microbial enzyme-responsive inulin nanoparticles for colon-targeted oral delivery of 5-ASA toward improved therapy of inflammatory bowel disease.
papers.abstract: Colon-targeted delivery of 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA) offers an effective strategy for treating inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) while minimizing systemic side effects. However, conventional oral 5-ASA formulations suffer from premature drug release and poor colon specificity. To overcome these limitations, we developed a biodegradable, prebiotic, and immunomodulatory inulin nanoparticle (INP) platform enabling microbial enzyme-responsive and site-specific release of 5-ASA in the colon.
papers.summary: The authors developed biodegradable inulin nanoparticles that release 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA) specifically in the colon in response to microbial enzymes, addressing premature drug release and poor colon specificity of conventional oral IBD therapies. The inulin carrier is itself prebiotic and immunomodulatory, potentially providing additional therapeutic benefit beyond drug delivery.

papers.title: Effect of quorum quenching enzyme YtnP on immune response and intestinal microbiota in Aeromonas hydrophila-infected grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon idella).
papers.abstract: Aeromonas hydrophila induces tissue swelling, necrosis, ulcers, and hemorrhagic septicemia in grass carp, causing significant economic losses. Quorum sensing, a communication mechanism among microorganisms, plays a key role in microbial ecological competition and dynamic equilibrium. Quorum quenching has emerged as a hot spot in anti-bacterial infection research. In this study, grass carp (n = 75 per group) were intraperitoneally injected with A. hydrophila and the quorum quenching enzyme YtnP. The expression levels of immune-related genes were assessed by qPCR. The intestinal microbiota was s
papers.summary: This study investigates whether the quorum quenching enzyme YtnP can mitigate Aeromonas hydrophila infection in grass carp by modulating immune gene expression and gut microbiota. The authors injected fish with the pathogen and enzyme, then measured immune-related gene expression via qPCR and characterized intestinal microbial communities. The findings suggest YtnP influences both the host immune response and microbiome composition during infection.
